documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE - OUTSIDE HOSPITAL
Date of service: 05/18/2026

CC: upper abdominal pain, black stools

HPI: 38 y/o M with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, ADPKD and Buerger disease. Burning pain in the upper abdomen for about 2 months. Comes on a few hours after he eats, eases for a while if he eats again or takes an antacid. For the last week his stools have been dark. No vomiting, no hematemesis, no lightheadedness or syncope. Takes ibuprofen on and off for muscle and night pain.

PMH: AATD with emphysema, ADPKD, Buerger disease, tobacco use.
PSH: tonsillectomy as a child.
Home meds: albuterol inhaler prn. Ibuprofen OTC occasionally.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD with ESRD; mother emphysema/COPD; older brother AATD.
SH: 1 pack per day cigarettes. No alcohol.

Vitals: within normal limits throughout, see flowsheet.
Exam: alert, comfortable. Abdomen soft with mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding or rebound. Rectal: dark brown stool, guaiac positive. Lungs diminished at bases. Healing fingertip and toe ulcers.

Labs: CBC normal, hemoglobin within range. BMP unremarkable apart from creatinine just above range, in keeping with his known polycystic kidney disease.

Course: Hemodynamically stable. GI consulted and performed upper endoscopy this afternoon (see GI report): 1.2 cm lesser-curvature gastric ulcer, biopsied. Observed overnight; tolerated diet, no further bleeding, hemoglobin stable on repeat. Discharged 05/19 in the morning.

Diagnosis: gastric ulcer with bleeding.
Discharge plan: omeprazole 40 mg twice daily. Stop ibuprofen and all NSAIDs. Biopsy results to PCP and GI. See PCP within 1 week. Return for vomiting blood, fainting, or black stools that worsen.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ESOPHAGOGASTRODUODENOSCOPY - OUTSIDE HOSPITAL GI
Date: 05/18/2026
Indication: epigastric pain, melena, guaiac-positive stool; NSAID use.
Sedation: moderate, monitored. Tolerated well.

Findings:
- Esophagus: normal.
- Stomach: a single 1.2 cm clean-based ulcer along the lesser curvature of the gastric body, no visible vessel, no active bleeding. Surrounding mucosa mildly erythematous. Biopsies taken from the ulcer edge and from antrum and body for H. pylori.
- Duodenum: normal to the second portion.

Impression: gastric ulcer, lesser curvature, 1.2 cm, no stigmata of recent hemorrhage requiring treatment.
Recommendations: PPI twice daily; avoid NSAIDs; follow biopsies; treat H. pylori if present; repeat EGD in 8-12 weeks to document healing.
NKDA.
Gastroenterology

reports.text:
Specimens: A. gastric ulcer edge, biopsy. B. gastric antrum and body, biopsies.
Microscopic: A. Ulcer edge with granulation tissue and fibrinopurulent debris; adjacent mucosa with chronic active gastritis. B. Chronic active gastritis with numerous curved rod-shaped organisms on the surface epithelium, confirmed by immunostain as Helicobacter pylori. No intestinal metaplasia. No dysplasia. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Gastric ulcer edge and gastric mucosa with Helicobacter pylori-associated chronic active gastritis. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

events.reason: Repeat upper endoscopy for gastric ulcer healing

documents.title: Repeat upper endoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ESOPHAGOGASTRODUODENOSCOPY - OUTSIDE GI
Date: 08/11/2026
Indication: follow-up of 1.2 cm lesser-curvature gastric ulcer (05/2026), H. pylori treated with bismuth quadruple therapy.
Medications: omeprazole 40 mg daily; albuterol prn; acetaminophen prn.
Sedation: moderate. No complications.

Findings:
- Esophagus normal.
- Stomach: the prior ulcer site on the lesser curvature has healed, leaving a small flat scar with converging folds. No active ulcer. Biopsies of the scar and of antrum and body.
- Duodenum normal.

Impression: healed gastric ulcer.
Plan: await biopsies (healing and H. pylori status). If negative, PPI may be stopped by PCP provided NSAIDs remain avoided.
NKDA.
Gastroenterology

reports.text:
Specimens: A. gastric scar, lesser curvature, biopsy. B. gastric antrum and body, biopsies.
Microscopic: A. Gastric mucosa with mild regenerative change consistent with a healed ulcer site. B. Gastric mucosa without active inflammation. Immunostain for Helicobacter pylori negative. No intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Healed ulcer site. No Helicobacter pylori. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
